title: expo/skills: agent skills for Expo apps, including the paid EAS ones
friendlyTitle: expo/skills: instructions that teach a coding agent how to build Expo apps
summary: expo/skills is on today's GitHub Trending list, with about 212 stars in the day and about 3,500 overall. It is an MIT-licensed pack of skills that teach a coding agent how Expo work is done. The names split the free framework skills (expo-) from the paid Expo Application Services skills (eas-). A separate experiments plugin holds APIs that are not final.
friendlySummary: This repository is on today's GitHub Trending list. It gained about 212 stars today and has about 3,500 in total. It is a pack of instructions, under the MIT license, that teach a coding agent how Expo app work is done. Names that start with expo- are for the free framework. Names that start with eas- are for Expo's paid services. A separate experiments pack covers tools that are not finished yet.
whyItMatters: Install the plugin in Claude Code or Codex, or add the skills with npx skills for Cursor, Copilot, and similar tools. The skills are instructions. The Expo MCP server, bundled with the plugin, is what lets the agent read current docs, install compatible packages, start an EAS build, and pull TestFlight crash data. Expo's own docs and CLI remain the source of truth. A skill that starts with eas- is a paid service, not part of the free framework.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Install the plugin in Claude Code or Codex, or add the instruction files to Cursor, Copilot, and similar tools. The files tell the agent what to do. A separate connection, included with the plugin, lets the agent read the current Expo docs, install matching packages, start a cloud build, and pull crash reports from TestFlight.
